title: U.S. House · Michigan's 10th District
area: Southern Macomb County, including Sterling Heights, Warren and Rochester Hills.

context.text: This is an open seat: incumbent John James (R) is running for governor of Michigan rather than seeking re-election. James was elected 48.8%-48.3% in 2022 and 51.1%-45.0% in 2024. Both the Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee and the National Republican Congressional Committee are targeting the district; as of August 2026 the Cook Political Report rated the race Lean Republican, though it moved to Toss-up by September 2026.

candidates.name: Christina Hines

summary.text: Christina Hines is the Democratic nominee for Michigan's 10th District. A Macomb County native, she worked as a prosecutor in Wayne and Washtenaw counties and ran unsuccessfully for Macomb County Prosecutor in 2024. She is running on lowering costs for families and protecting Social Security and Medicare/Medicaid from federal cuts.

background.text: According to her campaign website, she grew up in Macomb County in a middle-class family and attended Warren Woods Public Schools; she and her husband, David, are raising their children in Macomb County.
Attended the University of Michigan and earned a law degree from Wayne State University Law School.

Worked as a prosecutor immediately after law school. Her campaign website says she has prosecuted hate crimes, cold-case sexual assaults, homicide, torture and human trafficking cases in courts from the district level to the Michigan Supreme Court.

According to a news report, she was an assistant prosecuting attorney in Wayne County before heading the Special Victims Unit in Washtenaw County. Ballotpedia's race summary describes her as a former prosecutor and law professor.
Ran for Macomb County Prosecutor in 2024 against incumbent Peter Lucido, receiving 43% of the vote to his 57%, according to a news report.
Announced her candidacy for Michigan's 10th District in April 2025, after incumbent John James said he would run for governor; won the Democratic primary on August 4, 2026.
Says she is the only candidate in this race who grew up and still lives in Macomb County.
background.quote: As the only candidate in this race who grew up and still lives in Macomb County, I know firsthand the toll that reckless policies coming out of Washington have taken on our community.

priorities.text: Lowering the cost of groceries, childcare, housing, healthcare and energy, and raising the minimum wage.
priorities.quote: I'll work to lower the cost of essentials like groceries, childcare, housing, healthcare, and energy... I will also work to increase the federal minimum wage and expand paid family leave.

priorities.text: Protecting Social Security, Medicare and Medicaid from federal cuts.
priorities.quote: Cuts to Social Security, Medicare, Medicaid, and education, the haphazard firing of federal workers, and the rollback of environmental protections... all have real consequences.

priorities.text: Rebuilding the National Labor Relations Board and supporting the PRO Act; declines corporate PAC money.
priorities.quote: I do not take corporate PAC money, and I support a ban on members of Congress trading individual stocks... I will fight to rebuild and strengthen the National Labor Relations Board and support pro-worker legislation like the PRO Act.

positions.summary: Supports increasing the federal minimum wage.
positions.quote: I will also work to increase the federal minimum wage and expand paid family leave.

positions.summary: Says she will push back against Department of Homeland Security policies she says destabilize families, while also citing border security and the fentanyl crisis among community priorities.
positions.quote: I will push back against Department of Homeland Security policies that destabilize families or target communities unfairly.

candidates.researchNotes: No biography gaps beyond birth year and exact dates of her prosecutor positions, which public sources reviewed do not give.

candidates.name: Michael Bouchard

summary.text: Michael Bouchard is the Republican nominee for Michigan's 10th District and a U.S. Army and Michigan National Guard veteran who has not previously held public office. Raised in Michigan and the son of the Oakland County sheriff, he is running on manufacturing jobs, border security and 'back to basics' education.

background.text: Born in Michigan. His campaign website describes him as a third-generation Michigander and the son of Oakland County Sheriff Mike Bouchard.
Graduated from Michigan State University's ROTC program.
Served in the U.S. Army and the Michigan National Guard. His campaign website says he served in the 82nd and 101st Airborne Divisions, including missions to the southern border and Iraq.

According to his campaign website, he was chief operations officer for a 1,200-soldier infantry battalion in the Michigan Army National Guard and later a member of a joint task force in the fight against ISIS, for which he received the Bronze Star.
Says he led missions on the southern border during the first Trump administration.
Described by Fox News as a political newcomer who has not held office before; won the Republican primary on August 4, 2026, after endorsement by President Donald Trump.

priorities.text: Bringing manufacturing jobs back to Macomb County and cutting regulation on small businesses.
priorities.quote: I support President Trump's efforts to protect Michigan manufacturing, defend American jobs, and ensure that our workers... shape the future of our economy.

priorities.text: Finishing the border wall and ending 'catch-and-release.'
priorities.quote: I stand for finishing the wall, restoring the 'Remain in Mexico' policy, and ending catch-and-release once and for all.

priorities.text: A 'Parents' Bill of Rights' giving parents more say in what schools teach.
priorities.quote: In Congress, I'll back a Parents' Bill of Rights, so moms and dads always have a say in what their kids are being taught.

positions.summary: Supports finishing the border wall, restoring the 'Remain in Mexico' policy, ending catch-and-release, and deporting people he describes as 'criminal illegals.'
positions.quote: We must secure the border, stop the flow of illegal drugs, and deport criminal illegals who endanger our citizens.

candidates.researchNotes: Birth year and civilian employment history are not given in the sources reviewed.

candidates.name: Kwabena Nkromo

summary.text: Kwabena 'Cubby' Nkromo is the Green Party candidate on the November ballot for Michigan's 10th District. Ballotpedia lists him as a business consultant; in his Ballotpedia survey he describes himself as a civic leader, food-policy advocate and Green Party organizer.

background.text: Graduated from South Boston High School and attended Tuskegee University and Clemson University.
Career experience includes working as a business consultant.

In his Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey, describes himself as a grassroots civic leader, food-policy advocate and Green Party organizer with more than three decades of experience in community organizing, food systems, public policy, small business and ministry.
Nominated at the Green Party convention on July 18, 2026.

candidates.researchNotes: Biography draws on Ballotpedia and his self-written survey; no other profile or campaign biography page was reviewed.

candidates.name: Mike Saliba

summary.text: Mike Saliba is the Libertarian Party candidate for Michigan's 10th District and a repeat Libertarian candidate, having appeared on Michigan ballots in 2018, 2020, 2022 and 2024.

background.text: Born in Clinton, Michigan.
Ran for Michigan State Senate District 10 in 2018 and for U.S. House in Michigan's 9th District in 2020, losing both general elections.
Ran for U.S. House in Michigan's 10th District in 2022 and 2024; in 2024 he received 1.3% of the vote as the Libertarian candidate.
Nominated at the Libertarian convention on June 28, 2026.

candidates.researchNotes: Little biographical detail (education, employment) is available in sources reviewed.

candidates.name: Andrea Kirby

summary.text: Andrea Kirby is the Working Class Party candidate for Michigan's 10th District and has appeared on general-election ballots for U.S. House in 2018, 2020, 2022 and 2024.

background.text: Ran for U.S. House in Michigan's 9th District in 2018 and 2020.
Ran in Michigan's 10th District in 2022 and 2024; in 2024 she received 2.6% of the vote as the Working Class Party candidate.
Nominated at the Working Class Party convention on June 6, 2026.

candidates.researchNotes: No birthplace, education, employment history or campaign biography was found in sources reviewed.
